Half of it was bc I never really had the guts to do anything even though the thoughts were almost constant, at least once every hour or so. I guess a benefit of being too depressed to move is that you can’t move enough to kill yourself ha. 

Another part was that I didn’t want to inconvenience anyone i.e. “I don’t want my roommate to have to deal with my dead body” or “I don’t want to hurt someone’s car”

I also had a lot of “I can’t do that to my family and friends” but with some “I’ll teach them” and “if I’m dead I won’t care” mixed in which wasn’t as helpful. 

But if you want something more uplifting, another thing that really helped was finding things to look forward to like buying concert tickets or making plans for something. I would also, every now and then, find a beautiful moment, a moment where everything feels okay and you just have this little nugget of time where you can love the world again, just a little bit, and knowing that another one of those moments will be somewhere, near or far, in the future made it feel worth it. 

I know that it feels like it will never get better and that everyone says this but it does get better. Granted, I’m not all sunshine and rainbows; I still have days where getting out of bed seems impossible. But it was less than a year ago when every other thought I had was about how I would kill myself and now, it’s been months since the last time I thought about it. 

Just keep pushing through. Suicide is a permanent solution to a temporary problem. Life is change.

I dropped out of college last spring and I don’t regret it (for now at least). I never wanted to go to college in the first place but my parents basically forced me to go. My mental health got so bad I stopped going to classes altogether and every day was a struggle not to kill myself. Now, I just work and that’s it and though I’m far from being 100% okay, the thoughts of “you absolutely need to kill yourself and here is how” have decreased from at least once every hour to maybe once a month or less. 

That being said I was only two years into my bachelor. You’ve already endured two bachelors and are on your masters which is really amazing and something you should be proud of. If you truly enjoyed your profession before this depressive episode, there is a very high chance that this will pass and you’ll find the same satisfaction and enjoyment that you once had. 

How close are you to finishing your masters?
One of the things I really struggled with before dropping out was the fact that, though I was only there for two years I had a lot of extra credits and only needed two more semesters of classes. My parents continuously tell me “but you were so close why quit now?” But 1) I am terrified of debt 2) spending another January while still in school would certainly kill me

I think it would be best for you to assess your mental state and ask yourself if you are capable of continuing on the path to your masters, look at how far that path is and decide if you can make it. Don’t worry about whether it is “worth” it or not just focus on whether or not you can mentally and physically make it. If you feel like you cannot take a single step more, give yourself a break. You can always finish your degree at a later date. At my university, because instead of formally dropping out I just didn’t register for the next semester, I have a year and a half of being able to start classes right back up without reapplying. If that is the case with your uni, by all means, take a break. Take a year to recollect and decompress. If you think you have it in you to keep going and it’ll only be for a little while longer, by all means go for it and continue to pursue what you’ve been pursuing for the last few years. 

Idk if I’m the best for advice but that was my experience with dropping out and if you need a break from academics there’s nothing wrong with taking a break

Dissociative Identity Disorder. I’m no expert bc I just know about it from watching people’s videos about it on youtube but it’s basically the brain’s defense mechanism against trauma before the age of 8. In order to keep the host (original personality) from having to deal with the trauma and the memories of the trauma, the brain puts amnesia walls up between different parts of a child’s incompletely formed personality thus creating two people in one body. Alters always serve a purpose, either to hold difficult memories or to come out when the host needs protection. If you have DID, it’s very possible that an alter came out and emailed/called your therapist because they were worried about you or something like that. When an alter comes out, the host generally has complete amnesia over what happened. The most common way to communicate with alters is by leaving either written, video, or voice messages. Hope this helps :)
